# How to Lock In Lower AI Costs with Reserved Capacity

You’ve just finished a big project using your favourite AI tool—only to open the bill and wince at the surprise charge. It happens to the best of us. But what if you could set a fixed price for the AI power you actually need, and stop leaving your budget to chance?

Reserved capacity (also called provisioned throughput) lets you do exactly that. Think of it like booking a gym membership instead of paying every time you step on the scale. You pay a set rate for guaranteed access, and the more you use it, the better the deal.

## What is reserved capacity?

- **Reserved capacity** – a way to book a slice of an AI model’s processing power ahead of time. You pay a lower per-token rate because you’re committing to use it regularly.
- **Token** – a small piece of text, like a word or part of a word. AI models read and write tokens, and pricing is often shown per thousand tokens.
- **Inference** – the moment the AI actually processes your request and generates a response.
- **SLA (Service Level Agreement)** – a promise from the provider that your reserved capacity will be available 99% of the time, so you’re not left waiting when you need it most.
- **Frontier models** – the latest public AI models (like MiniMax M3 or GLM-5.2) that anyone can access without special licences.

In short, reserved capacity turns unpredictable AI costs into a predictable expense you can plan around.

## Setting up your reserved capacity (step by step)

### Step 1 – Pick a provider that offers reserved capacity
Most major AI platforms now include this in their dashboard. Look for a section called **“Reserved Capacity”**, **“Provisioned Throughput”**, or **“Commitment Plans”**.

### Step 2 – Choose your model
Select the model you want to use regularly—MiniMax M3 for creative writing, GLM-5.2 for multilingual tasks, or another frontier model.

### Step 3 – Decide how much capacity you need
You’ll be asked to specify a **tokens-per-second rate**, such as “300 tokens per second”. If you’re unsure, start small—you can always increase it later.

### Step 4 – Set your token pricing
The provider will show you a lower per-thousand-token price compared to pay-as-you-go rates. This discount comes from your commitment.

### Step 5 – Activate the reservation
Click **“Reserve”** or **“Enable Reserved Capacity”**. The system locks your capacity and starts billing at the agreed rate.

### Step 6 – Connect your app or script
You’ll receive an **API key**—a secret code that lets your program talk to the AI. Use it the same way you’d call any API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.provider.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"MiniMax-M3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a 100-word product description for wireless earbuds"}]}'
```

Your request now runs on your reserved capacity, so response times stay stable and costs stay predictable.

## Practical ways to use reserved capacity

- **Weekly blog writing** – Draft posts and newsletters without worrying about a sudden bill spike.
- **Student study sessions** – Summarise lecture notes or generate practice questions; the fixed token price keeps study budgets in check.
- **Small business marketing** – Generate product descriptions or social-media captions in bulk, knowing the cost won’t jump if you run a larger batch.
- **Creative projects** – Use MiniMax M3 for story outlines or GLM-5.2 for multilingual subtitles; the fixed capacity means you can experiment freely.

## What this means for you

### In everyday life
- **Predictable bills** – No more “I didn’t expect that many tokens” surprises. You pay a known rate for the tokens you actually use.
- **Lower cost** – Reserved pricing can be up to 70–80% cheaper than pay-as-you-go APIs, freeing up money for other hobbies or tools.
- **Reliability** – The 99% SLA means the AI will be there when you need it, whether that’s a quick recipe suggestion or a late-night study session.

### For work or a small business
- **Budget-friendly scaling** – As your marketing team ramps up content creation, the cost per token stays flat, making financial planning easier.
- **Fast, consistent response times** – No waiting for shared resources to free up; your prompts get answered promptly, keeping productivity high.
- **Simplified ops** – No need to calculate GPU hours or manage servers; the provider handles the hardware, you just set the token limit.

### If you’re just getting started
1. Sign up for a free trial with a provider that lists “Reserved Capacity”.
2. Reserve a modest 100-tokens-per-second capacity.
3. Send a single test prompt (e.g., “List 5 features of wireless earbuds”).
4. Check the billing tab after a day to see how the token price compares to on-demand pricing.

## Wrap-up

Reserved capacity turns the sometimes-unpredictable world of AI inference into a predictable, affordable service you can rely on daily. By booking capacity in advance, you lock in cheaper token rates, guarantee uptime, and remove the headache of managing GPU resources. Today, try reserving a small amount of capacity on your favourite AI platform, run a couple of test prompts, and see the cost savings for yourself. Happy prompting!
